frameworkName: MITRE ATLAS (Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems)
licenseNote: MITRE ATLAS content is publicly available. Summaries below are original interpretive content written for this application, not reproductions of ATLAS's text.
demonstrationSubsetDisclaimer: This is an illustrative subset for portfolio demonstration purposes, not full framework coverage.

controls.title: Reconnaissance resistance for model and system details
controls.summary: The vendor limits the information an attacker could gather about its AI system's architecture, model type, or training data through public sources or system responses.
controls.validationGuidance: Look at whether error messages or API responses reveal internal model details unnecessarily.

controls.title: Resource development and access control to training pipeline
controls.summary: Access to model training infrastructure, datasets, and pipelines is restricted and monitored to prevent unauthorized use or tampering.
controls.validationGuidance: Confirm the training pipeline has access controls equivalent to production systems, not treated as a lower-security internal tool.

controls.title: Adversarial example / evasion attack resilience
controls.summary: The vendor has tested the model's resilience to adversarial inputs specifically crafted to cause misclassification or evasion of intended controls.
controls.validationGuidance: Relevant primarily for classification or detection models (e.g. fraud, content moderation) where evasion has direct security impact.

controls.title: Model inference API abuse protections
controls.summary: Rate limiting, query monitoring, or anomaly detection is in place on inference endpoints to detect model extraction or membership inference attempts.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for monitoring of unusual query patterns (e.g. systematic probing), not just standard rate limiting for cost control.

controls.title: Data poisoning detection in training pipelines
controls.summary: The vendor has controls to detect anomalous or manipulated data entering the training or fine-tuning pipeline, particularly from external or user-generated sources.
controls.validationGuidance: Especially relevant for systems that incorporate user feedback or interactions into ongoing model updates.

controls.title: Supply chain integrity for pretrained models and dependencies
controls.summary: The vendor verifies the integrity of pretrained models, libraries, and ML frameworks used, reducing risk of a compromised upstream component.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask whether model checksums or signed sources are verified before use, similar to software supply chain practices.

controls.title: Detection and response plan for AI-specific attacks
controls.summary: The vendor's incident response plan explicitly addresses AI-specific attack scenarios (model theft, poisoning, adversarial evasion), not only conventional IT incidents.
controls.validationGuidance: This overlaps with AI-MAN-2 in NIST AI RMF - a single well-built incident response plan can satisfy both if it genuinely covers AI-specific scenarios.
